doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Lyrics and being in the moment
title: Finish That Lyric game
summary: Rowe quizzes Gates on vocalese lyrics, including Gimme That Wine and There I Go, with a Moody aside and Gates's own One Two Three Four Five Six Seven.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It is. Okay. Well I have a game show scenario for you.
Seventeen.
How did you know?
I just kind of took a wild guess.
This is “Giacomo Gates plays Finish That Lyric.”
Okay.
Okay, so I’m going to vocalize something to you, and we’ll start with something easy. Gimme that wine —
Gimme that wine. Yeah. What?
Okay what comes next?
Unhand that bottle.
Gimme that wine. Unhand that bottle.
I can’t get loose. Though I can’t cut loose without my juice.
That’s right. What is that, gotta have hot Lucy.
Yeah. When I go walkin’.
When I go walkin’. That’s right. Okay. Here’s an old ballad. The very thought of you makes my heart sing.
Oh yeah. I know it but I can’t tell you.
Yeah. Okay. Now this is one I think you’ll know. There I go, there I go, there I go.
There I go again. Pretty baby, you are the soul that stops my control. Yeah. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-
James Moody said a funny thing about that song, that the reason he played the intro the way he did is cause he was playing it on alto when he normally played it on tenor or something.
Was it a borrowed horn or something?
A borrowed horn or something, and he was feeling his way through it. I love that stuff. Okay how about this one? One two three four five six seven.
Steps to heaven.
Yeah, but it’s also your own thing.
Oh that one. One two three four five six seven. How many things do you need? Eight nine and ten or eleven, or is it just greed?
Money and cars.
Big apartments. What does it take to have fun? Too many things make my head spin. Better to have one.
